subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: Should hook-created sessions gain a dedicated lifecycle policy, and which default preserves existing persistent-session and transcript expectations?
rationale: Generic maintenance bounds storage eventually, but completion deletion, delayed cleanup, visibility, and transcript retention create new compatibility and data-retention semantics that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Add opt-in hook lifecycle
options.body: Introduce a default-off hook policy with explicit completion or TTL cleanup and transcript handling, preserving current behavior for existing configurations.

options.title: Use generic maintenance only
options.body: Document session.maintenance as the supported cleanup mechanism and decline another hook-specific configuration surface.

options.title: Unify ephemeral sessions
options.body: Design a shared task-scoped ephemeral-session contract for hooks and cron instead of adding a hook-only lifecycle policy.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in hook lifecycle
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-off hook policy with explicit completion or TTL cleanup and transcript handling, preserving current behavior for existing configurations.
